absent: Numeric values and defaults for idle tuning controls, calculation limits, leak allowance, timeouts, queue capacity and bounce interval.
Full layouts of platform and driver state records, firmware call blocks, file operation tables and wait queues.
Semantics, signatures and error encodings of firmware and power helpers not routed in this lane.
Ordering rules and irq-safety contracts for the registry lock versus control mutex and device suspend paths beyond what the fragments show.
Exact display selector meanings and console blanking integration outside the tried selectors and state mapping.
Processor context save and restore coverage and real-mode trampoline code behavior after the jump.

findings.text: Exposes a generic idle fallback used when firmware idle is unavailable or undesired; it places the processor in a halted state while keeping local interrupt handling quiescent.

Provides a non-returning platform restart service that records reboot intent in nonvolatile platform state under lock, installs a trampoline address space, then transfers control to low-memory firmware-adjacent code with the requested restart selector; the low-level transfer differs between 32-bit and 64-bit builds.

Provides a helper that installs the trampoline paging root before leaving protected mode and then discards all cached translations including global ones, with an extra translation-feature cleanup on 64-bit capable processors.

After installing the trampoline paging root, no stale global cached translations remain observable; on 64-bit capable hardware a translation feature that would break the later mode exit is dropped before the root is installed.

Adaptive idle policy re-evaluates firmware-idle eligibility only after a configured quiet window, disables it after overlong gaps or explicit prohibition, otherwise enables it when recent sleep share exceeds a threshold, then loops until rescheduling is needed with bounded retry allowance for firmware idleness, falling back to the generic halt, and announces busy on exit if firmware idle was ever used.
Power-off entry chooses between a processor-pinned firmware restart path and a direct transition to the off state, isolating firmware paths with processor affinity expectations from the generic path.

Power-management enable and engage operations maintain cached BIOS state flags for disabled and disengaged conditions, reject redundant transitions with distinct status results, and otherwise propagate firmware call outcomes while updating the cached flags to match the requested direction.

Power-status retrieval reports line, battery and lifetime components split from firmware registers, with special handling for broken firmware, missing errors, and a byte-order quirk that also marks the lifetime unit, while callers further split version-dependent flag and time-unit subfields.

Each opener carries validation identity, linkage into a global registry, capability and access-mode markers, circular notification storage with separate producer and consumer positions, independent tallies for outstanding versus consumed standby and suspend requests, plus a blocking-wait flag and outcome slot for suspend callers.

A global registry spin lock guards user list linkage and per-opener queue indices and pending tallies during enqueue, completion broadcast, insertion and removal; a separate platform lock guards the reboot-intent register update; a mutex serializes standby and suspend control operations against concurrent event handling.

Suspend and standby lifecycles bracket the firmware state transition with device and core quiesce and resume phases, preserve and restore processor context around suspend, optionally reprogram the platform timer on configurations that need it, normalize firmware success variants, log failures, and for suspend broadcast a synthetic resume notification and complete all waiting openers with the outcome.

Event processing drains firmware notifications until empty, suppresses bounce-period duplicates after resume, coalesces repeated suspend indications while one is outstanding, queues standby and suspend for user acknowledgement and only acts when no acknowledgement remains, clears suspend coalescing on any resume while optionally hiding synthetic resumes, forwards power-change indications to users, ignores time updates, and never refuses critical suspend.

Device file operations validate opener identity on every path, allocate and register state on open with privilege and mode derived from credentials and open mode, block interruptibly for queued notifications on read with nonblocking and size checks, expose readability via poll, require privilege for control commands that either acknowledge outstanding requests or inject user-initiated ones and possibly block for suspend completion, and on release fold outstanding counts back and unlink and free the opener.

Startup pins execution to the boot processor, caps negotiated firmware interface version with fallback on failure, conditionally enables and engages management, installs power-off and display-blank handlers on eligible configurations, then loops with timed sleeps dispatching events until stopped.

Notification storage can silently discard the oldest entry on overflow with only a one-time diagnostic; display blanking retries only once after engaging the interface; firmware idle refusal and missing-event conditions fall back to generic handling; periodic busy indication is rate-limited while acknowledgements remain outstanding.

Display power handling tries multiple display selectors in order, treats either success variant as completion, stops immediately when the interface is not engaged, and on first such failure attempts to engage the interface once before retrying, otherwise records the failure.
Reboot intent is expressed by writing value 0x00 to CMOS register 0x0f using NMI-disabled selector 0x8f.

Status reporting exposes driver version string, BIOS version split into major and minor bytes, BIOS capability flags, AC line state, battery state, battery flag byte on newer interfaces, charge percent with unknown sentinel, and remaining lifetime with unit selector distinguishing minutes from seconds and unknown sentinel.

Power-status sentinels use 0xff for unknown line, battery and flag bytes, negative one for unknown percent and time units, 0xffff for unknown lifetime, high bit 0x8000 to select minutes versus seconds, and low fifteen bits for the lifetime magnitude.
Firmware interface negotiation caps supported version at 1.2 and treats 1.0 as fallback, with behavior gates distinguishing versions above 1.0 for busy, reject and extended status handling.
